The '''1949 German football championship''', the 39th edition of the [[German football championship]], was the culmination of the [[1948–49 Oberliga|1948–49]] [[Association football|football]] season in [[Germany]]. [[VfR Mannheim]] were crowned champions for the first time after a one-leg knock-out tournament. It was both sides' first appearance in the final.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stokkermans |first1=Karel |last2=Werner |first2=Andreas |title=(West) Germany - List of Champions |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=3 June 2024 |date=14 April 2024}}</ref><ref>[http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/vfr-mannheim/1/ VfR Mannheim » Steckbrief] {{in lang|de}} Weltfussball.de – VfR Mannheim honours, accessed: 22 December 2015</ref>

The tournament was expanded so that ten teams were to take part in the final stage which was played as a one-leg knock-out tournament, with the matches played on neutral ground. The five regional Oberliga winners, along with [[VfR Mannheim]] and [[Wormatia Worms]], automatically qualified for the quarter finals, while the remaining three teams played qualifying rounds to clinch the eighth place.

The 1949 championship was the first to see a new trophy for the champions awarded. The pre-[[Second World War]] trophy, the ''[[Viktoria (trophy)|Viktoria]]'', had disappeared during the final stages of the war and would not resurface until after the [[German reunification]]. The new trophy, the ''[[Meisterschale]]'', was not ready for the 1948 season but was finished in time to be awarded to the 1949 champions.<ref name="Vic" >[https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=1000660 Die "Viktoria"] {{in lang|de}} ''DFB'' website – The "Viktoria", accessed: 30 December 2015</ref><ref>[https://www.dfb.de/historie/trophaeen/meisterschale/ Meisterschale] {{in lang|de}} ''DFB'' website, accessed: 30 December 2015</ref>
